en: 5. The Fifth Chapter on Knowledge (1) The Great Summary on the Emanation of the Yoginī Tantras and Others.
Homage to the glorious Kālacakra!

Homage to him, the sole teacher of the universe and the guru of gods, humans, asuras, and serpents—he by whom the Mind-born [Kāmadeva] was drawn from his own thunderbolt and brought to his own forehead by Śākyamuni through the power of the wisdom of insight (*prajñājñāna*), [becoming] the Great Uṣṇīṣa-vajra; he for whom there is both the non-substantial emptiness with an object and the non-objective great compassion.
Having bowed to that non-dual [reality] which is designated as Kālacakra— [in which] there is no cause, no characteristic, no movement, and likewise no succession—

Having prostrated with my head before that Tathāgata, the Primordial Buddha (Ādibuddha), who is without parts and whose four bodies—the Emanation, Enjoyment, Excellent Dharma, and Pure—are expressed by the syllables beginning with *ka*— [The verse continues: ...the pure body of the excellent Dharma, the enjoyment body, and the emanation body, along with the [pure] body, are declared as the four bodies within the syllables beginning with *ka*. Having bowed my head to that Tathāgata, the Ādibuddha who is without parts...
The commentary on the *Śrījñānapaṭala* is indeed being written by Puṇḍarīka, as urged by Mañjuśrī and having been prophesied by the Sugata.
By me, as the emanation-body Lokeśa holding a lotus,
for the sake of attaining the fruits of merit and wisdom for all beings, including the sages.

Here, in this glorious Malaya garden to the south of Kalāpa village, at the conclusion of the eastern gate of the Śrī Kālacakra maṇḍala palace, in the jeweled pavilion, King Yaśas—whose body was an emanation of Mañjuśrī and who sat upon a great lion throne of precious jewels—being requested by the Brahmin-sage Sūryaratha, spoke the request of Sucandra from the *Paramādibuddha* regarding the Knowledge Chapter (Jñānapaṭala) and the Tathāgata’s reply in the first verse: “O Lord, that sādhanā which you have spoken, together with the Supreme Victor, has indeed been partially understood. O Teacher of gods and men, I desire to hear further about the maṇḍala according to the divisions of the elements, and the six families of the Buddhas as they reside in the vowels and consonants of the six Yoginīs. Having heard the words of Sucandra, the Lord of Victors speaks concerning the maṇḍala and so forth, beginning with the elements.

Here, in the first verse, the request by Sucandra to Ādibuddha and the Tathāgata’s reply are chanted by Mañjuśrī as a refuge in the meaning; that very [text] is now expanded upon by means of this commentary, beginning with the words "something" (*kiñcit*) and so forth.

Here, regarding the *Sādhanapaṭala*: "O Śākyamuni, Teacher of gods and men! That which was spoken by you—the sādhanas of the Lord together with Kālacakra and the Tathāgatas—that has been understood by me in some measure."

Therefore, I desire to hear further regarding the Kālacakra maṇḍala within the body according to the divisions of the elements—that is, according to the purities of the elements such as bone and so forth. Furthermore, I desire to hear of the six families of the Buddhas, which have entered into the vowels beginning with *a* and the consonants beginning with *ka*, as will be explained; likewise for the six Yoginīs.
Just as there are six families for the six aggregates (*skandhas*), so too are there six families for the six elements, which have entered into the letters beginning with *ā* and so on.

Having heard these words of Sucandra, the Lord of Jinas then spoke: "The four bodies, beginning with the *sahaja*, are the nature of the aggregates (*skandhas*) and so forth, which are free from obscuration; their Lord, the progenitor, is the Perfectly Awakened One, the *Ādibuddha*.
The 'elements, maṇḍalas, and so forth' refers to the six families (*ṣaṭkula*) and other topics to be explained hereafter.
Thus ends the connection between the teacher and the requester.
In this verse, the request of Sucandra is made by means of the first three quarters; from the fourth quarter until the conclusion of the chapter, it consists of the Tathāgata’s response.
Furthermore, there is no further request—this is the rule in this tantra.

Now, the purification of the maṇḍala through the purification of the elements is described: Construct the pillars and the vajra-fence, as well as the circle of the earth and the wall, from the bones; and from flesh, blood, water, and fire, perform the application of colors for the deities of the directions—Indra, Yama, Kubera, and Varuṇa. From bile, make the sun; likewise, from phlegm, the moon; and from the sinews, the lotuses. [Draw] the five lines of the enclosures arising from earth, water, fire, wind, and space.
"Columns," and so forth.
Here, by means of the bones of the body, one should form columns within the body, that is, within the *kāyamaṇḍala*, through such a mental construction (*kalpanā*).
Likewise, the connection with the three verses is that one should form the vajra-fence, the earth-circle, and the wall as well, using the bones.
With this purification, one should cast bone powder and so forth into the midst of the colored powders (*rajas*).

Regarding "with the purifications of flesh, blood, and water": with the purification of flesh, the application of color occurs in the east; with the purification of blood, the application of color occurs in the south, at Yama; with the purification of water, the application of color occurs in the north, at Dhanada (Kubera); with the purification of feces, the application of color occurs in the west, at the other [Varuṇa];
and in the center, the application of color occurs with the purification of semen.
Where there is the sixth passion (*rajas*), there is the descent of colors through the purification of that passion.
Thus, through the purification of the flesh and other constituents of the Tathāgatas, there are six [deities] in due order: Amoghasiddhi, Ratneśa, Amitābha, Vairocana, Akṣobhya, and Vajrasattva.

By "bile" is meant the bile constituent (*pittadhātu*), and by "phlegm" is meant the phlegm constituent (*śleṣmadhātu*); these correspond respectively to the seats of the sun and the seats of the moon.
He also [made] the moon from sinews;
the lotuses from the cords [of the body]; and the seats for the moon and sun from the five lines of the ramparts.

The first line is by Kṣitijayā through the purification of the thumb; the second by Toṣajayā through the purification of the index finger; the third by Vahnijayā through the purification of the middle finger; the fourth by Vāyujayā through the purification of the ring finger; and the fifth by Ākāśajayā through the purification of the little finger. Thus, draw the five enclosure lines in the powder maṇḍala.

The Great Chapter on the Pervasion of the Yoginī Tantras and Others: The lotus of the Lord [is formed] by the channel of time (*kālanāḍī*); the circle of moving fire and so forth by the skin and other [tissues]; the solar doors by the apertures; and likewise the arrangement of jewels by the rows of teeth.

The eight wheels located in the cremation grounds are formed by the nails of the fingers, which have reached the moving circles; and by the adamantine teeth situated in every direction and intermediate direction at the end of the mandala.
Regarding the statement "the lotus is the time-vein":
the lotus of the Hero is purified by the *avadhūtī*; the remaining [lotuses] are [purified] by the [channels] beginning with the *lalanā*, up to the seventy-two thousand sinews—this is the rule.
"By the moving circle of fire and so forth, and by the skins and other [elements].
Here, the circle of wind is represented by the skins; the circle of fire by the red-hot element; and the circle of water by perspiration.
"The gates of Akam" refers to the twelve gates, that is, the twelve apertures.

There are two ears, two nostrils, two eyes, one mouth, three apertures for urine, feces, and semen, and two in the pair of breasts—thus, make twelve apertures in the *rajo-maṇḍala* for the purification of the twelve apertures.
Whatever arrangement of jewels there is in the maṇḍala, such as necklaces and so forth, make that with rows of teeth.
Those which are the eight cremation grounds of the wheels, make those with the nails of the fingers; this is for the purification of the nails of the hands and feet.
"By means of the rays of vajra-light," it is said:
"Create the outer vajra-fence with the hairs of vajra-flames.
With the hairs extending in every direction, there is vajra-light at the perimeter of the maṇḍala."

Thus, indeed, the Body-Vajra is described as having various excellent qualities and the form of a mandala; the Speech-Vajra consists of the primordial vowels and consonants, appearing in the form of deities belonging to all the families of the Victors; the Mind-Vajra, consisting of the six voids, exists in the threefold states of existence as the singular form of the Leader; and thus, indeed, the Gnosis-Vajra is the destroyer of the fear of cyclic existence, whose very nature is that of the Universal Mother.

Thus, indeed, the body-vajra consists of the six elements, possessing excellent and diverse qualities through the divisions of earth and so forth; it is said to be in the form of a mandala—this is the rule for the mandala.
Now, the purification of the host of deities is described, beginning with "the speech-vajra" and so on.

Here, that which begins with the vowels is composed of vowels and consonants; the speech-vajra is the host of deities transformed from the vowels and consonants, together with all the families of the Victors.
By that, it is stated that the speech-vajra is indeed the form of the deity;
thus, "fashion that very thing as the form of the deity in the colored powder mandala.

Regarding "the mind-vajra by means of the six voids," this refers to the sixfold [vajra] through the purification of eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mental consciousness.
The mind-vajra becomes free from obscuration through the six voids of the objects such as form and so forth.
Make that which has entered the threefold existence, which is all-pervading and of the nature of the Leader, into one.

Thus, the wise one [perceives] the graspable mind—which has entered the threefold existence, whose own nature is the Universal Mother, which is the reflection of emptiness, which destroys the fear of cyclic existence, and which is liberated from all conceptual constructions.
"Make Prajñā the leader in the mandala.

Thus, within the body there are the elements of body, speech, mind, and gnosis; externally, according to the relative truth (saṃvṛti), there is the mandala, the host of deities, the leader, and the leaderess; and according to the ultimate truth (vivṛti), it is established as the Nirmāṇakāya, Sambhogakāya, Dharmakāya, and Sahajakāya.
ga. red-black; ca. anus;
ca. completely purified.
ga. By the Blessed One; ga. To be grasped; ga. Do so.
Thus, by means of the six voids, there is the Mind-Vajra.

Now, the six mantra-families are described: in the *Vimalaprabhā*, the families of the six classes beginning with *ka* arranged in sequence are, respectively, the Vajra, the Sword, the Jewel-Wheel, the Lotus, and likewise the Scissors for the Victors.

Furthermore, each single class is individually divided into five sub-divisions by the supreme Victors, according to the distinction of syllables, due to the nature of earth, water, fire, wind, and space.
[Regarding the phrase "of the groups of gnoses" (jñānavargāṇām) and so forth:

Here, there are six groups beginning with *ka*, namely *ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa,* and *śa*. Of these six groups arranged in their sequential order, the "families" (*kulāni*) are the symbols of the six Conquerors (*jināḥ*), such as the vajra and so forth. Among them, the vajra is the family of the *ka*-group; the sword is the family of the *ca*-group; the jewel is the family of the *ṭa*-group; the wheel is the family of the *ta*-group; the lotus is also the family of the *pa*-group; and likewise, the flaying knife is the family of the *śa*-group. Thus, "the two are exclusively so" is the rule for the families of the groups.
Furthermore, each single class is divided by the supreme Victors into five divisions.
Here, wherever there is one, there the five families exist according to the truth of origination (*samudayasatya*).
Therefore, by means of them, worldly activity is accomplished for the sake of mundane success.

And for this reason, each individual group is divided fivefold according to the distinction of its respective letters: due to the state of earth, the state of water, the state of fire, the state of air, and the state of ether; thus, each group is fivefold, namely *ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa*. || 5 ||

Thus, the vowels beginning with *a* have been recited according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*). Furthermore, by the method of individual phonemes (*pratyāhārapāṭha*), they are recited again according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) starting from space (*ākāśa*). These are stated as follows: In the supreme family of the Victorious One (*jinakula*), the groups of consonants beginning with *ka* are divided into five types: 1. **The divisions of Space (*ākāśa*)**: Even among the divisions of the void (*śūnya*), there are *ṅa, ña, ṇa, ma*, and likewise the first vowel (*a*) and the division of Wind (*vāyu*), which is the letter *i*. 2. **The divisions of Wind (*vāyu*)**: [The letters] *gha, jha, ḍha, bha, dha, śa*; the divisions of Fire (*vahni*) are those beginning with *t* (*ta, tha, da, dha, na, ṣa*). 3. **The divisions of Water (*ambhas*)**: The letter *u* is the division of Water; [the letters] *pa, pha, cha, ṭha, pha, tha* are the divisions of Earth (*bhūmi*). 4. **The divisions of Earth (*bhūmi*)**: Those beginning with *lṛ* (*la, va, ra, ya, ha, sa*). Thus, in the supreme family of the Victorious One, the groups of consonants beginning with *ka* are divided into these five modes.

Regarding "at the beginning" and so forth: here, first of all, although it is empty (śūnya), there are *ṅa*, *ña*, *ṇa*, *ma*, *mā*, as well as *ka*; furthermore, the vowel *a* is that which is without accent (*avisvara*).

By the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) that "that which falls within [a category] is included by the mention of that category," it is established that the letter *ha* is also a variety of space (*ākāśa*).
Similarly, the letter *i*, *gha*, *ḍha*, *bha*, *dha*, and *śa*, as well as *ya*, are varieties of air (*vāyu*);

*ṛ*, *ga*, *ja*, *ḍa*, *ba*, *da*, *ṣa*, and *ra* are varieties of fire (*vahni*); *u*, *kha*, *cha*, *ṭha*, *pha*, *tha*, *pa*, *va*, and *a* are varieties of water (*toya*); and *l̥*, *ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *pa*, *ta*, *sa*, and *la* are varieties of earth (*bhūmi*).

Thus, the consonant groups beginning with *ka* are divided by the five supreme *jita*-families; it is the rule that the letters beginning with *ṅa* are to be understood as belonging to the *vajra*, *khaḍga*, *ratna*, *padma*, and *cakra* families. (6)

Now the families of the Uṣṇīṣas are described: the Uṣṇīṣa consists of the five voids, and likewise the three families; the Vajras of body, speech, and mind; and the family of the primary mudrās. Indeed, all the consonant groups beginning with *ka* are joined with *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, and *la*.
*Bho sa ca. Bho sa.*
And it is said by him, "O sir, it is as if with five."
O, there is also "api" and "na". There is no "ṛ".

This is the Great Chapter on the Emanation of the Yoginī Tantras and so forth. Lokāloka consists of the vowels together with the consonants *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, and *la*. And Lokottara consists of the letters beginning with *ka*; indeed, it becomes the Lord of the Vidyādharas, comprising all the groups of letters situated in the eight peaks. ||7||
"Uṣṇīṣa," and so forth:
here, the Great Uṣṇīṣa family is that which is great; it is the five voids as described in the "Chapter on the World Realm.
The three families are the garments of body, speech, and mind, namely Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
"The first" refers to *a*, *i*, *ṛ*, *u*, *ḷ*;
"the family of mudrās" refers to the host of deities beginning with Akṣobhya for the purpose of sealing;
"the great family of Lokāloka" refers to the groups of consonants beginning with *ka* joined with *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, and *la*; and "all together" refers to the thirty-six consonants.

The groups beginning with *ha* and so forth, joined with *ha ya ra va la*, are sixty with their respective measures (*samātra*). The previously mentioned groups beginning with *ka* and so forth, with their respective measures, are three hundred and sixty. When these are further differentiated by *guṇa*, *vṛddhi*, and *yaṇādeśa* substitutions, they become one thousand and eighty. This constitutes the mundane and supramundane family (*kula*). O Lord of Vidyādharas, the consonants (*vyañjana*) are joined with the letters beginning with *ka*; thus, all the groups situated in the eight peaks (*aṣṭakūṭasthavarga*) are: *ka kha ga gha ṅa; ca cha ja jha ña; ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa; pa pha ba bha ma; ta tha da dha na; sa pa ṣa śa la va ra ya ha; la va ra ya kṣa*. (7)

Now, each individual tantra is described according to its respective initial syllable: The thirty letters beginning with *ka*, joined with *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, and *la*, together with *sa* and *kṣa*, become thirty-six when differentiated by the modifications of the vowels (*mātrā*). When multiplied by the six qualities (*guṇa*), these become the sixty-three Lords of the Wheels (*cakranātha*).
When surrounded by one limb and embraced by Wisdom (*prajñā*), he becomes the fivefold Lord of the Wheel; when surrounded by five, he becomes the ninefold Lord of the Wheel.
Regarding the passage beginning with "What thirty," etc.:

here, the thirty consonants beginning with *ka* together with *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, *la*, *kṣa*, and *sa* are indeed thirty-six; these are the phonemes (*varṇa*), and those phonemes are differentiated by the modifications of the vowels (*mātrā*).
The vowels beginning with *a* consist of twelve short and long measures (*mātrā*). There are twelve substitutes for the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* stages, and twelve *yaṇ*-substitutes.
Being differentiated by these six sets of six modifications of measure, they become "six times six" or "six multiplied by six," thus resulting in thirty-six Lords of the Wheel (*cakranātha*);
that is, each individual phoneme becomes differentiated into thirty-six forms.

Of all these, there are thirty-six; thus, in the thirty-six tantras, the lords of the wheels (*cakranātha*) also exist in the form of the thirty-six consonantal places. First, the *Kavajra-tantra* is spoken of by means of the leader of the *ka*-consonant. In that mandala, the leader has one limb and is differentiated by a single measure (vowel). The *ka*-consonant, together with the letter *a*, constitutes the "Single Hero" (*ekavīra*).
"Surrounded by two" means he is joined with two instances of the letter *a*; thus the leader becomes embraced by Wisdom (*prajñā*). This is the *Ka*.
"The fivefold self stands with the five," thus [it is] *kā ki kṛ kukla*; the Lord of the Wheel (*cakranātha*), surrounded by nine, is the ninefold self, [thus] *kā ki kī kṛ kṝ ku kū klū klṛ*. || 8 ||
The Yoga Tantra of the Pa-ka Yoginī. ||9||

The number of *mātrās* consists of thirty-three and nine directions, totaling thirty-six; the door-keepers are formed by the letters beginning with *ya*, while the remainder of the entire host of *gaṇas* is formed by the remaining *mātrās*. The six *Krodhas* arise from the letters beginning with *ha*, situated in the directions of their own families through the divisions of the *vāyu-mātrā*s and so forth. In each case, according to the division of the phonemes (*varṇa*), the number of *mātrās* is sixty-three and nine directions, totaling thirty-six.

In that regard, the previously mentioned thirteen-fold self, when joined with these *yaṇ*-substitutes—*kya, kra, kva, kla*—becomes thirteen-fold; furthermore, when divided by the *guṇa* vowels along with the gatekeepers (*dvārapāla*), it becomes nineteen-fold: *ka, ke, kara, ko, kala, kam*. Then, together with the *vṛddhi* vowels, it becomes twenty-five-fold: *kā, ke, kār, ko, kāl, kaḥ*. Finally, together with the "womb-wisdom" (*garbhaprajñā*), it becomes thirty-two-fold: *kahā, kyā, kā, kvā, klā, kahāḥ*.

Then, *kaṃ* joined with *kaḥ* consists of thirty-four aspects; likewise, *khaṃ* joined with *vaḥ* consists of thirty-six aspects. Thus, in all cases, there are thirty-seven aspects, with the syllable *hūṃ* in the center as the leader (*nāyaka*), and the thirty-six maṇḍala-deities being *ka kā ki kī kṛ kṝ ku kū klṝ klṝ kaṃ kaḥ*.
A phoneme (*varṇa*) is distinguished by short and long vowels, as in:
*ka, kā, ke, kai, kar, kāra, ko, kau, kal, kāl, kaṃ, kaḥ*; likewise, a phoneme is distinguished by *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* [vowel] substitutions, as in:
*vaha, kahā, kya, kyā, kra, kā, kva, kvā, kla, klā, kahaṃ, khaḥ*; and a phoneme, such as the letter *ka*, is distinguished by short and long *yaṇ*-substitutions.
The vowels (*khādi*) are also thirty-six each;
thus, the tantra beginning with *Khavajra* is said to consist of consonants (*kavyañjana*) divided into thirty-six measures (*mātrā*).
In this way, the Lord of the Mandala is the essence of the six Śivas.
Regarding "the gatekeepers by means of the vowels": the gatekeepers are formed by the consonants accompanied by the *yaṇ* substitutes—namely, *kya, kra, kva, kla*.
By these [consonants], the entire family of aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*) is [represented].
By the remaining vowels—those in the positions of the short, long, *guṇa*, and *vṛddhi* [vowels]—[the same is signified].
By means of the remaining vowels alone—namely *hā* and so forth—the six Krodhas arise;

thus, where there are ten Krodhas in the ten directions, there the other six Krodhas are formed by those [vowels] beginning with *hā* through the substitution of the long vowels (*yaṇādeśa*), resulting in *vaha*, *vahā*, *kā*, *kvā*, and *klā*.

Where there is a Lord of Krodha (*krodheśa*), there are twelve Krodhas, including *vaha* and *vahaḥ*. This is the rule for the six divisions of the *Kulatantra*; even in the *Ekakulatantre*, it is according to the distinctions of the six measures (*ṣaṇmātrā*) of the *Kula*.
"In this way, the space element (*ākāśadhātu*) is situated above, belonging to its own family, while the gnosis element (*jñānadhātu*) is situated below.
The other deities are situated in the east, south, north, and west according to the divisions of air and so forth.

Thus, each consonant, beginning with *ka*, is divided by the distinctions of vowels and the distinctions of colors; it is divided into thirty-six types, as in "taste multiplied by taste. Regarding "the Yoga-tantra of the Yoginīs": that in which there is the movement of the Yoginīs and the Leader is immovable is, conventionally speaking, the Yoginī-tantra. That in which there is the movement of the Means (*upāya*) and Wisdom (*prajñā*) is immovable is the Upāya-tantra."
In its essential nature, the entire Yogatantra consists of wisdom (*prajñā*) and means (*upāya*).
Thus it is said in the *Hevajra*: "By the syllable *he* is meant great compassion; 'vajra' is said to be wisdom.
Listen as I proclaim to you that Tantra which consists of wisdom and means. What [is this]?

From here on, the "Great Chapter on the Emanation of the Yoginī Tantras and so forth" is commenced once again. For, as it is stated in the *Samāja*: "The union of wisdom and means is designated as 'yoga';
the gathering (*samāja*) is declared to be the meeting of all the Buddhas. Because of this statement, this is not a tantra of means (*upāyatantra*).
Likewise, when one has thus awakened, yoga does not consist in the body of means nor in wisdom alone;
the Tathāgatas have declared that yoga is the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of wisdom and means. (9)

Thus, in each individual letter within the mandala multiplied by the [six] tastes, the Lord of the Mandala, through the aggregates, elements, sense-faculties, and so forth, along with the divisions of the Mothers, shall purify the entire host of the families of deities;

and the sealing of the deities occurs through the voids, the Unstruck (anāhata), and so forth, by means of all the families of the Victors, upon the seat in the center of the wheel within the uneven and even families, from the crown protuberance (uṣṇīṣa) down to the lotus. || 10 ||

Thus, each individual syllable is a flavor multiplied by flavors; in the *Yoginīyogatantre*, it is established that the Lord of the Mandala resides in every mandala. That which is the *Ekakulatantra*—namely the *Trikula* and *Pañcakula*—is itself divided into thousands, lakhs, and crores of varieties.
There is no limit to the number of tantras, such as the *Samāja* and others, or the *Hevajra* and others, due to the infinite inclinations of sentient beings; such is the rule of the tantras.
Now, the internal purity of the mantra-deities is described, beginning with the words "by the aggregates" (*skandhaiḥ*).
In this context, the fivefold self is purified by the five aggregates; the ninefold self is purified by the five aggregates together with the five elements, along with the four organs of action.

The thirteen-fold self is purified; with the six sense faculties, the nineteen-fold self is purified; with the six objects, the twenty-five-fold self is purified; when the five action faculties enter along with the activities of the five action faculties, it becomes the thirty-two-fold self together with the self-luminous wisdom (*svābhā-prajñā*); joined with the sixth action faculty and the activity of the sixth action faculty, it is the thirty-four-fold self; and joined with the six aggregates and the elements, it is the thirty-six-fold self.
Thus, the six aggregates, the six elements, the six sense faculties, the six objects, the six organs of action, and the six activities of the organs of action are the elements of the maṇḍala;
their pervader is the mind and gnosis, which are the leaders everywhere.
In this way, one should dry up the entire family of the assembly along with its fruits by means of the divisions of the Mothers.
And [the phrase] "by the empty ones, such as the Unstruck (anāhata) and so forth," does not exist here.
Sixth [chapter]:

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, the sealing of the deities through the purification of the six aggregates by means of the six voids—knowledge and so forth—and all the Buddha-families occurs at the crown protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*), up to the end of the lotus, within the uneven and even families, and upon the seat in the center of the wheel.
Here, in the crown wheel (*uṣṇīṣacakra*), Akṣobhya is in the *bindu* (the vowel *a*).

Thus, in the heart, within the maṇḍala of Rāhu, is Amoghasiddhi; on the forehead, within the moon maṇḍala, is Amitābha, *u*; likewise, in the unequal wheel (*viṣamacakra*) of the Unequal Family, Vairocana is at the navel in the fire of time (*kālāgni*, *la*); Ratneśa is at the throat in the sun (*ṛ*); and Vajrasattva is at the secret place in the maṇḍala of gnosis (*jñānamaṇḍala*, *aṃ*). This is the rule for the sealing (*mudraṇa*) of the deities. Furthermore, regarding the sealing of the body and the sealing of the vital breath (*prāṇa*), [the syllables] are to be assigned as follows: *la* at the navel, *u* at the heart, *ṛ* at the throat, *i* at the forehead, and *a* at the crown (*uṣṇīṣa*) within the maṇḍalas of earth and the other elements.

Likewise, in the sealing of the *cittabindu*: at the forehead is OṂ on the moon-maṇḍala; at the throat is ĀḤ on the sun-maṇḍala; at the heart is HŪṂ on the Rāhu-maṇḍala; and at the navel is HOḤ on the Kālāgni-maṇḍala. Furthermore, regarding the sealing with the *jñāna*: "The letter A is the mouth of all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen"—thus is established the sealing of body, speech, mind, and gnosis as the Vajramaṇi, A. || 10 ||
Now, the classification of the faces is being stated:

The differentiation of the Vajra-face arises from the divisions of the Mothers; the differentiation of the arms occurs through the principles (*tattva*), and likewise there is another differentiation of mudrās through the Body-Vajra and so forth.
In the Yoga Tantra of immeasurable qualities, there are thirty-six differentiations of color for each individual name of the male and female deities within the even and uneven families.
Regarding "by the Vajras" and so forth:
here, the single family, the triple family, the fivefold family, and the sixfold family are called "vajra";
thus, there is a threefold division of faces.

"Purified by one family, he has one face; purified by three families, he is pure with three faces; purified by five families, he becomes five-faced; purified by six families, he becomes six-faced and fearsome.
Thus, according to the rule of the Lord of Jinas in another tantra, from the eight-faced and so forth up to the hundred-faced Halāhala, the Leader becomes purified by as many elements as there are.

Likewise, in the *Sādhanapaṭala* of the *Kālacakra*, it is stated regarding the Lord of the Maṇḍala: "At the end of darkness [in the final stage], he possesses one to infinite faces and many hands and feet, and many colors," and so forth.
In this case, for the twenty-four-armed [deity], there is a differentiation of the arms according to the various Mothers:
*ha hā hi hī hṛ huhū*—these eight are black, arising from the quality of *tamas*;
*ha hā hai hai hara hār ho hau*—these eight are red, arising from the quality of *rajas*.

"h h hā hya hyā hra hā 'hvā"—these eight are white due to the quality of *sattva*; thus is the rule for the *Kālacakra* and likewise for Viśvamātā, who is yellow due to all qualities: "haṃ haḥ hala hala hala hāl hna hlā"—these eight are yellow by virtue of being the nature of the face of Gnosis (*jñānavaktra*). This is the classification of the *tattvamudrās*. "ā ī ṝ ū la aḥ"—this is the sealing (*mudraṇa*) of the entire host of deities according to the divisions of space, wind, fire, water, earth, and gnosis (*jñāna*).

Furthermore, there is likewise the sealing of the body with Oṃ, the sealing of speech with Ā, the sealing of the mind with Hūṃ, the sealing of gnosis with Hoḥ, and the sealing of the single family with the syllable A of the Unstruck (Anāhata).

Such is the sealing in six parts: by means of five families, four families, three families, and one family, within the thirty-six Yoga Tantras. In the infinite qualities and manifold varieties of colors, each individual Tantra has its own description and name: Ka-vatra, Kha-vatra, Ga-vatra, Gha-vatra, Ṅa-vatra, Ga...
May there be food for the bindu.
The Kālacakra born from the sky.
ca ha hā, ga hna hvā
What do you say?
What?
and wisdom as well.
And in the family and in division.
"In the chapter on the letters," verse.
This is the Great Chapter on the Pervasion of the Yoginī Tantras and so forth. Thus, [the rule applies] even to the thirty-six syllables beginning with *ca* and ending with *ya*.

"Equal family" (*samakula*) refers to the Wisdom Tantra (*prajñātantra*), while "unequal family" (*viṣamakula*) refers to the Means Tantra (*upāyatantre*). This is the rule for the sealing (*mudraṇa*) of deities and their consorts:
externally it consists of the *rucaka* and so forth; internally, it is "of the nature of the Buddhas. || 11 ||

Now, the purification of birth through the generation stage (*utpattikrama*) of the mantra-deities is described: The single seed-syllable becomes the solitary hero (*ekavīra*), who, in the state of passion (*rajas*), attains a state of equal flavor (*samarasa*) while embraced by Wisdom (*prajñā*). He is constituted of the five aggregates (*skandha*) and is further presided over by the nine [deities] consisting of the elements such as earth and so forth, and is encircled by the anus and other [orifices], the eyes and other [senses], and thus consists of twenty-five principles. In this way, at the emergence of the teeth, the Lord (*īśvara*)—possessing infinite wheels (*anantacakra*)—is again [manifested] by means of the teeth.
Regarding the passage beginning with *boje* and so forth:

here, just as at the time of conception (*garbhādhāna*), the single mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) together with the depositing of the *bodhicitta* becomes unified with the object-field of the *dharmadhātu* and is called the "Solitary Hero" (*ekavīra*), because his own consort (*svābhaprajñā*) is included within him; even so, by means of the single letter *ka*, the deity is established as the Solitary Hero. Subsequently, that seed becomes of equal flavor (*samarasa*) within the *rajas* and is embraced by the Wisdom (*prajñā*). From that impression (*vāsanā*), the aggregate of consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*) becomes embraced by the Wisdom; this is the rule, according to the application of the fourth state (*turyāyoga*), expressed by the syllable *kā*.

Thus, when the five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*) are produced, the embryo consists of five aspects; likewise, the deity also consists of five aspects: *kā ki kṛ ku kla*. Similarly, when the qualities of bone, fluid, heat, and movement arise, the embryo—presided over by the aggregates and elements (*skandhadhātu*)—consists of nine aspects; likewise, the deity is established as consisting of nine aspects: *kā ki kī kṛ kṝ ku kū kla klū*.

In this way, the completion of the speech, hands, anus, and feet, together with the previous aggregates (*skandha*) and elements (*dhātu*), consists of thirteen constituents during the completion of the action faculties (*karmendriya*). Just as it is for the child, so it is for the deity: *kā ki kī kṛ kṝ ku kū kla klu kya kra kva kla*.

Just as the internal object within the womb consists of nineteen constituents together with the previous aggregates and so forth, so too is the deity: *kā ki kī kṛ ka ku kū klū klū kya kra kva kla kā ke kār ko kāl kaḥ*.

Then, upon the arising of the eye and the other senses, just as the infant is born consisting of twenty-five principles, so too is the deity: *kā ki kī kṛ kṝ ku kū klū kla kya krakva kla kā kai kār ko kāla kaḥ kaṃ ke kar ko kala kam*.

Then, through the engagement of the five organs of action (*karmendriya*) in speech, grasping, movement, and the production of excrement and urine, the "child" (*bāla*) consists of thirty-two aspects; likewise the deity as well: *ka kā ki kī krū kṛ ku kū klu klu kha khā kya kyā kra krā kva kvā klaklā ka kā ke ke kar kāra ko kau kal kāla kaṃ kaḥ*. This is the accomplishment up to the age of twelve years.

Then, up to the age of sixteen, just as the fourth state (*turyā*) occurs for the child during the emission of semen (*cyavana*), that very [state] is the Fourth Body (*caturtha-kāya*). It is the sixth aggregate (*skandha*), the sixth element (*dhātu*), the sixth faculty (*indriya*), the sixth object (*viṣaya*), the sixth organ of action (*karmendriya*), and the sixth activity of the organ of action (*karmendriya-kriyā*).
Thus, there are six aggregates, six elements, twelve bases (*āyatana*), six organs of action, and six activities of the organs of action.
In this way, the thirty-six elements are the supported, while the thirty-seventh is gnosis (*jñāna*).
O Min-can by name!
And the Buddha-nature [is realized] in succession.
And the Svābhā [Kulikā] has entered the nature of the Fourth State.
And [the elements] within the internal self are the hands, feet, anus, and genitals.
O, what? What?
Ga-ca.
Kai kar ko ca bho.
There is no 'ka', there is no 'ga', and there is no faculty of action.

5, 10, 15, 20. The actions of the organs of action (*karmendriya*) are twelve: *ka, kā, ke, kai, kar, kār, ko, kau, kal, kāl, kaṃ, kaḥ*. Thus, the twelve sense bases (*āyatana*) are established. The leader of these elements is the Great Void (*mahāśūnya*) of five syllables, the means (*upāya*) which is the drop-void (*binduśūnya*) of six syllables. Wisdom (*prajñā*) is the syllable *vaṃ*, and the syllable *e*—thus the syllable *evaṃ*—is the leader, the Great Bliss (*mahāsukha*), the Lord of the Mandala (*maṇḍalādhipati*). As it is established in the *Kavajra-tantra*, so it is established in the *Khavajra* and other tantras.

Thus, the aggregates (*skandha*) and elements (*dhātu*) are in the inner enclosure, the twelve sense-bases (*āyatana*) are in the outer enclosure, and the doors are guarded by the sense-faculties of action (*karmendriya*) together with their objects.

Here, just as a prince becomes a sovereign with infinite wheels (*anantacakrī*) after the age of sixteen because he is the progenitor of the aggregates that are his sons and daughters, so too the five Tathāgatas, through the radiation of their divine arrays, become the Lord (*īśvara*), the leader of the host of deities, who possesses infinite wheels; this is the rule.

In this context, just as the body of the embryo is formed, so too in the formation of the deity, the *maṇḍalarājāgrī* is the limb of service (*sevā*); just as the speech is formed, so is the *karmarājāgra* the near-attainment (*upasādhana*); just as the drop of the bodhicitta is formed, so is the *binduyoga* the attainment (*sādhana*); and just as bliss arises from the emission of the semen, so is the *sūkṣmayoga* the great attainment (*mahāsādhana*).
Thus, the purification of these four-limbed attainments, as previously mentioned in the Inner Chapter, is to be explained in detail; such is the rule. || 12 ||

Now, the emanation of the family deities from the six elements within the six wheels is described: Amitābha, who is pure, from the perfectly pure water, white as the moon, marked with a lotus, and possessed of pride; Lokeśvara, who rides upon a horse-chariot; Māmakī, who is Rūpavajrā; Raudrī, the ocean, Gaṇendra accompanied by a brahmin and a serpent, and Salūkā with a tiger’s face—these were emanated by the Wielder of the Vajra from the glorious left face out of supreme compassion. (13)
"Pure," and so forth.

Here, just as for human beings after the sixteenth year there is a manifold radiation of the mind by way of the nature of the six elements (*ṣaddhātu*), so too is there such a radiation for the Leader (*nāyaka*) through the differentiation of the six elements. "Pure" refers to the forehead wheel (*lalāṭacakra*). From the aggregate of perception (*saṃjñāskandha*) of the element of water, which is called "thoroughly purified water" because it is free from obscuration, a host of deities radiates, white as the moon and marked with the lotus, such as Amitābha.

Māmakī, Padmāntaka, Acala, Mānī, Cundā, Lokeśvara, Rūpavajrā, Raudrī, Lakṣmī, Samudra, Gaṇendra, the Nāga Ananta, Kulika, Vyāghravaktrā, and Ulūkavaktrā—these deities are emanated with supreme compassion from the left face, that is, from the white face of the body. This is the rule for the Blessed One Kālacakra. Here, the host of deities is sealed by Amitābha as consciousness; marked by Amitābha with the lotus symbol, they grant the accomplishment of the rites of pacification and enrichment due to their white, water-like color.
Thus, the observation of the radiation and withdrawal of the immeasurable Bhakula deities is [the third aspect]. || 13 ||

Now, the radiation (*spharaṇa*) of the Amoghasiddhi family is described: In the Dharma [direction], from the perfectly pure wind element, there is Amoghasiddhi with a sword in his lotus-hand, as well as Tārā, Akṣobhya, Sparśavajrā together with Atibala, Carcikā, and Śṛṅkhalā.

[Paṭala, verses 12–16; Mahoddeśa on the Radiation of the Yoginītantras and so forth: The Nairṛta [direction], the Śūdra, and the Nāga—these, along with the Wind [direction], the Dog-faced goddess, and the Crow-faced goddess, have been emanated by the Lord of the Three Worlds from his eastern face with a mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī*). (Verse 14)
"Dharma," and so forth.

Here, in the heart, at the wheel of dharma (*dharmacakra*), from the element of wind which is perfectly pure and from the purified formative factor (*saṃskāra*), there arises a host of deities marked by the sign of a sword and black in color.

They are as follows: Amoghasiddhi, Tārā, Vighnāntaka, Nīladaṇḍa, Atibalā, Vajraśṛṅkhalā, Khagarbha, Sparśavajrā, Cāmuṇḍā, Vaiṣṇavī, Vāyu, Nairṛti, Padma, Karkoṭaka, Kākāsyā, and Śvānāsyā. These [arise] from the eastern face, that is, from the mind-face (*cittavaktra*).
"By the Lord of the Three Worlds, they are emanated with a mind of loving-kindness.

Here, the host of deities is sealed by the consciousness of Amoghasiddhi; [the deity] marked by Amoghasiddhi has the sword as his emblem and bestows the accomplishment of the rites of eradication and inciting hatred. He is black, according to the color of wind.
Thus, the emanation and withdrawal of the deities of the Amoghasiddhi family is performed through the execution of activities (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna*). || 14 ||

Now, the emanation of the Ratnasambhava family is described: In the Sambhogakāya, from the right face of the glorious Lord of the Universe, who is like the rising sun of pure fire, there are the Jewel-holder (Ratnadhṛk) and Pāṇḍarā; Bhūgarbha and Jambhaka; Varuṇa, Rasa, Kuliśā, and Śūkarī; the six-faced one and Agni; the two Kings, the two Lords of Serpents, the sow-faced one with a manifest frown, and Gṛdhra—these were emanated by the Supreme Joy. (15)
Regarding "in the *saṃbhoga* [mandala], from the pure fire":
here, in the throat-cakra, from the pure sensation (*vedanā*) comes the one who resembles the pure rising sun, red in color, and holding a jewel—namely Ratnasambhava.
Likewise [is] Pāṇḍarā.

Prajñāntaka, Ṭakkirāja, Jambhī, Bhṛkuṭī, Kṣitigarbha, Rasavajrā, Vārāhī, Kaumārī, Agni, Kārttikeya, Śūkarāsyā, Gūdhavaktrā, Vāsuki, and Śaṅkhapāla—these were emanated by the Lord of the Universe from the glorious right face with supreme joy. All are red in color, sealed by Ratnasaṃbhava, and bestow the accomplishments of subjugation and attraction, due to their nature as the speech wheel (*vākcakra*).
Thus, the emanation and so forth of the deities of the Ratnasaṃbhava family occurs through the wisdom of equality (*samatājñāna*).
Here too, Ratnasambhava is sealed by consciousness. || 15 ||

Now, the emanation of the family deities of Vairocana is described: O supreme lord of men, from the western face [of the central deity], there are the Sage Cakrapāṇi, who resembles excellent gold and resides on the perfectly pure ground of the navel; Viṣkambhin; Locanā; Gandhavajrā, who performs the rite of immobilization (stambhana); Mārīcī; Indrī; Śakra together with the four-faced one; and all the Vaiśyas, Nāgas, and so forth. Together with the Lord, they have been emanated for the welfare of all beings through the state of equanimity (upekṣā). (16)

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, it says: "At the navel of gnosis, from the perfectly pure earth," and so forth. Here, "at the navel" refers to the emanation wheel (*nirmāṇacakra*). From the pure aggregate of form and the pure earth element arises the Sage Vairocana, who has the color of refined gold, is yellow in hue, and holds a wheel in his hand;
likewise is Locanā.

Yamāntaka of great power, Stambhinī, Mārīcī, Viṣkambhin, Gandhavajrā, Aindrī, Brahmāṇī, Śakra, Brahmā, Takṣaka, Mahāpadma, Jambukāsthā, and Garuḍāsyā—these, for the benefit of all beings, were emanated from the western face by the Lord through equanimity. From the face of gnosis (*jñānavaktra*), they are yellow in color, marked with the wheel, bestowers of the accomplishment of activities such as paralyzing and deluding, and sealed by Vairocana;
Vairocana, moreover, is sealed by primordial wisdom (*vijñāna*).
Thus, the emanation and so forth of the Vairocana family proceeds from the mirror-like wisdom (ādarśajñāna). || 16 ||

Now, the radiation of the Akṣobhya family is described: From the pure emptiness at the crown of the head (uṣṇīṣa) arise the Holder of the Supreme Vajra (Akṣobhya) and Dhātvīśvarī; the two uṣṇīṣas are the Dharmadhātu and the Sky due to the power of their qualities, as are Vajrapāṇi and the others.

From the pure [emptiness] at the secret place arise all the treasuries of the bliss of peace, such as Śabdavajrā and the rest; they are radiated above and below, abodes of manifold virtues, for the sake of the liberation of living beings. (17)

"From the pure emptiness at the *uṣṇīṣa*": from the pure aggregate of consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*) and the pure space element (*ākāśadhātu*) in the *uṣṇīṣa*-cakra, there is Akṣobhya, the bearer of the supreme vajra, sealed with gnosis (*jñāna*), dark blue in color.
Likewise [is] Vajradhātvīśvarī.

The *uṣṇīṣa*, Vajrahaṃkāra, Raudrākṣī, the Queen of Wrath, Vajrapāṇi, Dharmadhātuvajrā, Viṣṇu, Yama, Jaya, and Nāga—these, abodes of manifold qualities, are emanated from the upper face of emptiness; they bestow the accomplishment of all activities, possess vajra symbols, are sealed by Akṣobhya, and are of a dark blue color like the sky.
Thus, the emanation and so forth of the deities of the Akṣobhya family is [effected] through the wisdom of the perfectly pure dharma-sphere (*suviśuddhadharmadhātujñāna*).
Now, the emanation of the Vajrasattva family is described: "In the secret [place], from the pure sun," and so forth.

Here, in the secret wheel (*guhyacakra*), from the aggregate of pure gnosis (*śuddhajñānaskandha*) and from the element of pure gnosis (*śuddhajñānadhātu*), there arises Vajrasattva, whose emblem is a blue three-pronged vajra, and who is sealed by consciousness (*vijñāna*).
Thus is the gnosis-element (*jñānadhātu*).

Prajñā, Nīla, Sumbharāja, Vajravega, Atinīlā, Krodheśvarī, Rudra, Jambhala, Samantabhadra, Śabdavajrā, and Vijayanāga—these have been emanated from the downward-facing gnosis-realm for the benefit of all people and for the sake of the liberation of living beings. From the perfectly pure gnosis of the dharma-sphere (*suviśuddhadharmadhātujñāna*), they are blue in color; they are sealed by Vajrasattva in the form of blue Akṣobhya, and they are the accomplishers of all activities.

Thus, the radiation of the six family deities within the six cakras and the performance of the welfare of the world is established as being accomplished through Kālacakra as the progenitor after sixteen years; this is the rule.
Here, Akṣobhya is sealed by Nīla in the form of Akṣobhya—the dark aggregate of consciousness (vijñānaskandha)—and the blue aggregate of gnosis (jñānaskandha) is [sealed] by the dark Akṣobhya.

Now, regarding the sealing (*mudraṇa*) according to the division of the four families of body, speech, mind, and gnosis: therein Vairocana is white by virtue of the nature of the moon; Amitābha is red by virtue of the nature of the sun; Akṣobhya is black by virtue of the nature of Rāhu; and Vajrasattva is yellow by virtue of the nature of the fire of time (*kālāgni*).

Now follows the great chapter on the radiation of the *Yoginītantra* and so forth, concerning the relationship between the support and the supported, which constitutes the sealing according to the procedure taught in the chapter on the means of achievement (*sādhana*).

For instance, Akṣobhya is the seal of Vairocana; Vairocana is [the seal] of Amitābha; Amitābha is [the seal] of Ratnasaṃbhava; and Ratnasaṃbhava is [the seal] of Amoghasiddhi—this is the rule for sealing.
Thus, the Great Lord of the Three Realms, who possesses infinite wheels, is to be understood in all other tantras within the three families and the five families. || 17 ||

Now, the radiation of the Wisdom Tantra (Prajñātantra) is described: On the petals of the cardinal directions are Locanā and the others; on the petals of the intermediate directions is a skull-cup filled with blood. Standing in the *pratyālīḍha* posture upon the sun atop the head [of Brahmā], he resembles a cloud at the end of an aeon (*pralaya*) and has trampled upon the Lord of Soma. Bound with a garland of skulls, his faces are like the oceans, and Heruka possesses arms as numerous as the sun. He wears a tiger skin as his garment and holds the hide and bones of the lordly elephant of the dissolution.
Regarding the passage beginning with "dikpatra" (the directions and petals):

here, in the *Cakrasaṃvara*, it is said that the four [deities] such as Vajraḍākinī and the others, as well as Locanā and the others, have the nature of earth and so forth, and bestow the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of pacification and so forth.

However, if they were differentiated by having black complexions and so forth corresponding to the mind-face and other [faces], they would not bestow the ritual accomplishments (*karmasiddhi*) of earth and so forth.

Thus it is said: "With yellow [color] one should perform *stambhana* (paralysis); with white, *śāntika* (pacification) on the earth; with red, *vaśya* (subjugation) and *ākarṣaṇa* (attraction); and with black, *uccāṭana* (expulsion) and so forth. Therefore, by virtue of her black color, Vajraḍākinī is the wind element (*vāyudhātu*); by virtue of her red color, Lāmā is the fire element (*tejodhātu*); by virtue of her yellow color, Khaṇḍarohā is the earth element (*pṛthvīdhātu*); and by virtue of her white facial color, Rūpiṇī is the water element (*toyadhātu*).

Just as the colors of the mind, speech, gnosis, and body faces are respectively black, red, yellow, and white, so too should the colors of the nine goddesses each—beginning with Pracaṇḍā—who reside in their respective directional divisions, be understood according to the *Mahālakṣābhidhāna*.
This is the rule of the Blessed One.
Therefore, for those of limited capacity, Mañjughoṣa has revealed that very same elaboration here in the *Kālacakra* by means of a concise instruction (*laghūpadeśa*).
Regarding the deities in the petals of the directions: in the western petal is Locanā by way of color; Khaṇḍarohā is yellow, by virtue of being the nature of the anal channel;
the western face of knowledge of Kālacakra and Heruka is yellow, by virtue of the nature of the earth element and their respective symbols;
in the northern petal is Rūpiṇī, white by virtue of the water element; the northern body-face is white, by virtue of being the nature of the lalanā channel.

In the south is Lāmā, red, because of the color of fire; her speech-face is red, because of the nature of the tongue. On the eastern petal is Vajraḍākinī, black, because of the color of wind; her mind-face is black, because of the nature of the urine-channel. Thus, by way of the nature of the avadhūtī, Vajravārāhī is dark-tawny, because of the nature of the śaṅkhinī.
The Lord Heruka, the Kālacakra-holder, is blue in color;

thus, on the spokes of the mind, speech, and body wheels, the Ḍākinīs are to be known as follows: in the east and southeast they are black, in the south and southwest they are red, in the west and northwest they are yellow, and in the north and northeast they are white—likewise, these goddesses are to be understood in the eight cremation grounds.

The expansion of these [channels], the extension of karma, and so forth, as taught in the Tantra, should be understood from the *Ṣaṭsāhasrikā-ṭīkā* composed by Vajrapāṇi; therefore, they have not been written here in this concise tantra.
The passage beginning with "entered into the six-petalled [lotus]" and so on is easy to understand.

Thus, the *Samāja* is also well-known and easily understood in the *Māyājāla-vimalaprabhā*; therefore, it has not been written here, as it consists merely of the radiation of the mind, speech, and body vajras.
Here, in the *Mūlatantra*, the characteristics of the *sūtras* are as follows: two, one, three, and a half; a half, indeed one, a pair, and the moon.
One yuga and one yuga-part [are assigned] to the thirty-two [spokes] and so forth;
the remainder, beginning with the rampart, is like the maṇḍala of Kālacakra.

Outside, there are three wheels with goddesses whose bodies are black, red, and pure white; likewise, there are six Vajras accompanied by the wrath-born (krodhajā) and element-born (bhūtajā) goddesses, who are two-armed and moon-faced.

At the gates are the Caṇḍas standing upon corpses, and in the intermediate directions are fixed the Heroines holding flaying knives and oyster shells. In the hands of the Heroes are the thunderbolt, the hand-drum, the vajra-khaṭvāṅga, and the bell.

On the circle of earth and water in the eight directions of Śrī Meru, one should know the locations of all the *pīṭhas*, *upapīṭhas*, *kṣetras*, *chandohas*, *melāpakas*, and *citibhuvanas*, as well as those of Fire and Wind, situated in this manner within the country and city in every cardinal and intermediate direction. This teaching, known as the *Prajñātantra*, was emanated from the eastern face by the Guru of the three worlds.

In the center is a nine-part wheel within the lotuses of the moon and sun, fashioned from half a portion of the mandala with a vajra pillar and a surrounding rim, presided over by the deities of the great aggregates and elements;

on the outer wall of the enclosure are the objects and subjects seated upon moon and sun seats, while the gatekeepers are situated on the sun, and the family of the other retinue is all around on the pedestal.

Thus, although six types have been described, likewise in the Yoga Tantra and the *Samāja*, there are the Wrathful Deities in the corners; on the sides are the sense objects and their subjects; Jambhala with grain in his hand; speech, feet, hands, and anus; the vulva, the anus, and the moon; and those whose nature is the channels of time (*kālanāḍī*).

The entirety of wisdom and means, manifested from the right face as having three faces and six arms, becomes a wheel within the triangle at the center, O Lord of Men; it indeed occupies one-third of the mandala. Furthermore, in the subsequent enclosure, there are the eight deities presiding over the elements and aggregates, beginning with Śabdavajrā.
Within the external maṇḍala, the host of wrathful deities is fixed in the ten directions situated upon the sun; on its wall-enclosure are all the Bodhisattvas, numbering four times the oceans.

This is the great chapter on the radiation of the Yoginī-tantras and so forth. The Māyājāla, which has three divisions, three faces, and six arms according to the distinctions of the deity's body, is that which was initially emanated from the left face by means of the dull-heartedness of the entire [assembly].

O King, here in this *Mahāsaṃvara* tantra, which is doubled by being permeated with yoga, the *ḍākinīs* are expanded through the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*), the six families (*ṣaṭkula*), and the cremation grounds (*citibhuvana*) from the western face.

Having laid out the mandala with threads according to the six parts of the six openings, situated within the moving circles, one should [draw] the lotus petals from the center in divisions of six by six, joined with half the pericarp (*karṇikā*).

The artisan should fashion a row [of ornaments] with lotuses, jewels, and excellent vajras; the turret and the door with twelve [parts], and the vedikā and the hārabhūmi with six parts, each divided into two.

With five [parts] he should make the lines of the five walls, and with three the fillet at the base of the hāra. With twelve [parts] the wing and the cheek, and with thirty-six [parts] the archway atop the pillar.

One should construct eight doors in each cardinal and intermediate direction for this circular Great Maṇḍala; in its center is a multicolored lotus, and upon its pericarp is a seat composed of the sun and moon. There is a blue wheel and a blue garland; the earth is green, and the ground is black with a yellow wheel. The earth is red with a white wheel, and the ground is white with a red garland and a red wheel.

The ground is yellow and blue, and it may also be white and dark-colored; the wheel is divided into six parts, and the ground for the limbs is according to the pleasure of the progenitor. Likewise, there are two sets of eight cremation grounds on the outside according to the families, and likewise eight goddesses in the interior. There are eight skull-cups filled with the essence of nectar upon the petals, and the goddesses are on the eight petals.

Externally, there are the goddesses Lāsya and the others in the cardinal and intermediate directions, as well as the eight great nāga kings; outside of that are the circles of earth, water, fire, and wind, and the vajra-fence.
(28) In the *Vimalaprabhā*, it says "by the threads of knowledge," and so forth.
Here, from the western face, the face of gnosis (*jñānavaktra*), the *Mahācakrasaṃvara* is twice the size of the *Tricakrasaṃvara*, because it consists of six wheels and sixteen cremation grounds;

therefore, its mandala is circular for the purpose of purifying the eight doors. Hence, the characteristics of this mandala are stated: "by means of lines divided into six apertures" refers to a division into ninety-six parts; "situated within the moving circle" refers to the wind-circle at the end of the four hundred thousand *yojanas* of the world-system.
Regarding "in the body, with those [lines] reaching four cubits":

having laid out the mandala with ninety-six lines, one should construct each wheel in the center by means of six divisions; thus, the wheel consists of six divisions. Furthermore, the lotus-garland is joined with half of the pericarp (kaṇikā) by means of six divisions.
Thus, there are forty-two divisions in the east; likewise in the west, south, and north. Altogether, eighty-four divisions have been accounted for.

Of the remaining twelve divisions out of the ninety-six, the eastern ground consists of six divisions, and the western ground is the same; likewise in the left and right—thus the lines in all directions are pure. Therein, within the previously mentioned six divisions, the lotus petals are formed by four [divisions] and the half-center (kaṇikā) by two.

Thus, in the wheel of the gnosis element (*jñānadhātucakra*), there are four spokes for the wheel and two for the row of insignia; in the center of the pericarp (*kaṇikā*) and so forth is a sixteen-petaled lotus; outside the lotus petals is a blue row of pericarps, the ground of which is dark green; likewise, the spokes of the wheel are also blue.
Then, in the earth-element wheel, the row of wheels is yellow and the spokes of the wheels are likewise [yellow]; the ground at the base is black.
In the water-element wheel, the row of lotuses is white and the spokes of the wheels are [white]; the ground at the base is red.
In the fire-element wheel, the row of jewels is red and the spokes are [red]; the ground at the base is white.
In the wind-element wheel, there is a black garland of swords and yellow wheels; the ground at its base is yellow.
In the space-element wheel, there is a dark-blue garland of vajras and wheels; the ground at its base is blue.
Then, the colored ground consists of six parts, according to the face of the progenitor.

In the east and southeast [the wheel] is black; in the south and southwest it is red; in the west and northwest it is yellow; in the north and northeast it is white. The door-wheels are likewise. Thus, there are eight great cremation-ground wheels at the ends of the eight doors; the eight cremation-ground wheels are also within the eight doors. In this way, there are sixteen cremation-ground wheels with eight spokes. On the petals of the central lotus are eight goddesses; on the eight petals are skull-cups filled with nectar. Between the eight goddesses, upon the six-wheel eight-spoked [mandalas], are the forty-eight goddesses of the *pīṭhas*, *upapīṭhas*, and so forth.
In this way, the heroes are to be understood:

on the outer altar (vedikā) are the eight Nāga kings; at the base of the arch-pillars are Lāsyā and the others; and the remaining characteristics of the doors and so forth are to be understood as being like those of the Kālacakra maṇḍala. (25–28)

Now, the seed-syllables of the goddesses within the six wheels beginning with *ca* are described: The long and short vowels, along with the consonants *sa*, *ta*, *pa*, *ṭa*, *ca*, *ka*, and *kṣma*, and so forth, correspond to the voids (*śūnya*) and other elements; they are associated with the spokes of the wind-wheel and others. By virtue of the movement of the sun, they are long on the spokes starting from the top, having the nature of the elements beginning with earth (*kṣmā*). By virtue of the movement of the moon, they are short on the spokes starting from the top. At the head of each respective wheel, at the door, and in the interval between doors, the groups of consonants (*savarga*), joined with *ha* and *kṣa*, reside in the expanse of the sky. (29)
Regarding "long" and so forth:
the long vowels are *lū*, *ū*, *ṛ*, *ī*, and *ā*;

and by the short vowels *bha*, *i*, *ṛ*, *u*, and *la*—these [vowels] differentiated from the six classes (*varga*) of *sa*, *ta*, *pa*, *ṭa*, *ca*, and *ka*—the letters beginning with *kṣma* and the void (*śūnya*) and so forth reside upon the supports of air as "long."

Here, the Wisdom Wheel (jñānacakra) is presided over by the deity Savarga. Its spokes are as follows: *slū* in the northwest (vāyavya), *pū* in the northeast (īśāna), *ṣa* in the southwest (nairṛtya), *śī* in the southeast (āgneyī), and *kā* in the netherworld (pātāla). *Vāyavya* is in the center of the cremation ground wheel (śmaśānacakramadhya). These five Ḍākinīs are the mistresses of the five maṇḍalas in the sign of Scorpio (vṛścikalagna); they are the carriers of the vital breath (*prāṇavāha*) of all sentient beings according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) through the right nostril. Then, in the sign of Sagittarius (dhanurlagna), [the flow is] upwards: *ka* in the northwest, in the center of the western cremation ground wheel; *śi* on the eastern spoke of the Wisdom Wheel; *ṣū* in the south; *pu* in the north; and *sḷ* in the west. This is the flow of the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*) in the sign of Sagittarius.
Then, in the Earth-wheel (*pṛthvīcakra*), the *tavarga* is the presiding deity (*adhidaiva*).

Its [phonemes] are: *tla* in the northwest (*vāyavya*), *thū* in the northeast (*īśa*), *dṛ* on the southwest spoke (*nairṛtyāra*), *dhī* in the southeast (*agni*), and *nā* in the underworld (*pātāla*).
At the gateway of the northwest (*vāyavya-tla*) is the center of the cremation ground wheel (*śmaśānacakra*)—thus, in the sign of Virgo (*kanyā-lagna*).
Likewise, on the top of the scale (tulā), there is no [letter]; at the western gate is *dhi*, at the eastern is *dṛ*, at the southern is *ḍa*, at the northern is *thu*, and at the western is *slū*.
Then, in the wheel of the water element (*toyadhātucakra*), the *pa*-group is the presiding deity (*adhideva*):

its *pla* is in the northwest (*vāyavya*), *phū* in the northeast (*īśa*), *bṛ* in the southwest (*nairṛtya*), *bhī* in the southeast (*agni*), and *mā* in the underworld (*pātāla*) at the northeast gate.
Thus, in Cancer Lagna, these are the presiding deities; likewise, in Leo Lagna, *ma* is in space (ākāśa), *bhi* at the eastern gate, *bṛ* in the south, *phu* in the north, and *plu* in the west.
Thereafter, in the Fire-wheel (Tejaścakra), the *ṭa*-group is the presiding deity.

In that [mandala], *ṭla* is in the northwest (*vāyavya*), *īśe* (the northeast) is *ṭhū*, *ḍṛ* is in the southwest (*nairṛtya*), *ḍho* is in the southeast (*agni*), and *ṇā* below is at the southwest gate; thus, in the sign of Taurus (*vṛṣa-lagna*).
Then, in Gemini (*mithuna*), *ṇa* is above; at the southern gate in the cremation ground (*śmaśāna*), *ḍhi* is in the eastern spoke, *ḍū* in the south, *ṭhu* in the north, and *dala* in the west.
Then, in the wind-circle (*vāyu-cakra*), the *ca*-group is the presiding deity (*adhidaiva*).

In its moving Vāyavya [spoke], there is *ī*; in Īśāna, *chū*; in Nairṛtya, *ju*; in Agni, *jhī*; and in the netherworld (pātāla), *trā*. In the Fire-gate at the Cancer ascendant (*mīnalagna*), then, at the Aries ascendant (*meṣalagna*), *tra* is above. In the cremation-ground wheel (*śmaśānacakra*) of the Eastern Gate, in the Eastern spoke (*pūrvāra*), there is *jhi*; in the South, *jū*; in the North, *chu*; and in the West, *cūla*. Then, in the wheel of the space-element (*ākāśadhātucakra*), the guttural class (*kavarga*) is the presiding deity (*adhideva*).

In its northwest spoke is *klū*, in the northeast *khū*, in the southwest *gu*, in the southeast *ghī*, and below is *ṅā*. On the cremation ground wheel (*śmaśānacakra*) in the middle of the southern gate of the southeast [mandala], during the Aquarius ascension (*makaralagna*), there is *ṅa* above.

Then, during the Aquarius ascension, in the middle of the eastern gate of the southeast [mandala], there is *ghi* on the eastern spoke; *ut* on the southern spoke; *ra* on the northern spoke; and *kla* on the western spoke.
Thus, at the gates and in the intervals between the gates, the groups of consonants (*sabarga*) joined with *ha* and *kṣa* are situated in the earth and the sky.

Here, for the six groups [of deities], there are twelve syllables—*dīrgha* and *hrasva*: *kā ka nā na mā ma ṇā ṇa ñā ña ṅā ṅa*—which are the carriers of the mandala of emptiness (*śūnyamaṇḍala*) for the twelve cremation-ground goddesses (*śmaśānadevī*).

Furthermore, according to the division of the four junctions (*saṃdhyā*), there are four syllables at the end of each of the three zodiac signs (*lagna*): *ha hā kṣa kṣā*. These are located in the four cremation grounds of the North (Vāma), East (Īśāna), South (Dakṣiṇa), and Southwest (Nairṛtya).
Thus, there are sixteen goddesses in the sixteen cremation grounds. In the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*), on the forty-eight petals of the womb-lotuses (*garbhapadma*), there are eight goddesses.

Their seed-syllables are: *a* on the eastern petal, *aḥ* on the southern petal, *aṃ* on the northern petal, *ā* on the western petal, *ha* on the southeast petal, *haḥ* on the southwest petal, *haṃ* on the northeast petal, and *hā* on the northwest petal. Thus, within the intervals between these eight petals are the eight skull-cups (*kapāla*).

In the center is Vajraḍākinī, and the Blessed Lord Heruka as Kālacakra, the leader, with the seed-syllables *hūṃ* and *phaṃ*. At the end of the seed-syllables of these ḍākinīs and ḍākas is the vajra; together with that, their names are [given], beginning with Śrīvajrā and ending with Klu’vajrā.
Due to the differentiation of their states of being (*bhāva*), there are forty-eight ḍākas for these [ḍākinīs]: Śivajña, Sṛvajra, and so forth.
Regarding *gṛ*, *khu*, *kāna*, *nāma*, *māṇa*, *ṇāña*, *ñāṅa*, *ṅāyatra*, and *ḍākinībīja*:
wherever there is a long vowel (*dīrgha*), there the seed-syllable of the *ḍāka* is short; wherever there is a short vowel (*hrasva*), there it is long.
Thus, "the thunderbolt" (*stṛvajra*) and "the sword" (*sivatra*) represent wisdom (*prajñā*) and means (*upāya*).
"Pūvajrā, Bṛvatra"—
in this manner, the measurement of the chest is stated everywhere;
thus one should worship in the mandala, for it is the rule that the *Ḍākinījālasaṃvara* is double [that measure].
The placement (nyāsa) performed here in reverse order, beginning with Scorpio (Vṛścika), Sagittarius (Dhanu), and so forth, has been explained in detail.

Here, through the cessation of the twelve limbs (dvādaśāṅga-nirodha), the placement of the sacred seats (pīṭha) and secondary seats (upapīṭha) and so forth is performed in reverse order—starting from Sagittarius and Scorpio—from the perspective of ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya).

From the perspective of conventional truth (saṃvṛti), the placement of the secondary branches (upapīlava) and so forth is performed in the sequence of Capricorn (Makara), Aquarius (Kumbha), and so on, based upon the twelve limbs of dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda).

Just as in the *Tricakrasaṃvara*, there is one placement of the sacred seats (*pīṭha*) and so forth in reverse order by means of Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍākṣī, and the others, while the second is in direct order by means of Mahāvīryā and the others, along with the secondary cremation grounds (*upaśmaśāna*) and so forth; in this worldly convention, that which is the concealment (*saṃvṛti*) is to be known as the revelation (*vivṛti*).

Thus, in the supports of the winds, the long vowels are assigned according to the movement of the sun in the right channel by virtue of the movement of the vital breath (*prāṇa*), while in the upward movements, the short vowels are assigned according to the movement of the moon by virtue of the circulation of the *prāṇa* in the left channel; this is the stated sequence of placement.

Furthermore, by way of reversal (*saṃvṛtti*) starting from the *upapīlava* [asterism] and so forth, the long and short letters of the consonant groups *ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *pa*, *ta*, and *sa* are to be applied to the mandalas beginning with Capricorn (*makara*).

The consonants beginning with *ka* and so forth, differentiated by the vowels beginning with *la*, and the consonants beginning with *ka* and so forth, differentiated by the short vowels beginning with *a* through the divisions of the bow, the scorpion, and so on—thus, earth and the other elements [reside] on the spokes starting from the top in the right mandala according to the flow [of the breath], while space and the other elements [reside] on the spokes starting from the top in the left mandala according to the flow; this is the internal rule.

The *ḍākinīs* possess a short nature, have faces like the moon, hold a curved knife and a shell in their hands, stand in the *ālīḍha* posture, drink the blood of demons with their respective vessels, and are disheveled-haired and naked.

On the feet, waist, forehead, ears, throat, and hands are the bone-seals such as the *ghurghura*; on the head is a garland of skull-fragments; on the hip-surface are the five-colored [seals] of the Jinas. The two-faced *ḍākas* hold in their hands a skull-cup (*supavi*), a *ḍamaru*, a vajra, a *khaṭvāṅga*, and a bell. Around the neck is a garland of noble skulls (*śrīmuṇḍamālā*), and on the head is a crown with a vajra-band and a jewel.

There is a sacred necklace (*śrīkaṇṭhī*), the sound of anklets, a breast-plate (*rucaka*), a girdle, and earrings. A garland of incomplete skulls extends over the entire body; they have fangs and bear the ash-seal.

The consort of Māra wears a garland of skulls upon her head and a necklace of severed heads around her neck; she has a hundred faces, and a crescent moon rests upon her crown. She holds a leopard skin and an elephant hide at her waist, while at her feet are the orbs of the Moon, Sun, and Fire. Her body is smeared with ashes, and she bears the marks of the lords of serpents. Resembling the fire of universal destruction, the Ḍākinī kisses [her consort]; in the petals of the directions are Ḍākinīs holding large hand-drums (ḍamaru), vajras, and skull-staffs (khaṭvāṅga). In the intermediate directions are vessels of feces, urine, blood, and human flesh, and in her hand is a vessel of semen.

The Great Chapter on the Pervasion of the Yoginī Tantras and so forth: likewise, there are eight goddesses as well. The wheel of the attainment of the bliss of both is entirely yellow, white, reddish, black, green, and blue in body; their colors and hand-symbols in their respective directions are as before, in the family of the Lord and the Father of the Jinas. The net of three eyes and the mutual embrace are to be understood everywhere according to the power of one’s own and others’ families.

By means of various [elements] beginning with the aggregates, the elements, the objects, and the subjects, and by others beginning with the five sense-faculties, the directions, the earth, the intermediate directions, and the powers—the goddesses are to be purified along with the sons of the glorious Jinas.
The remaining five verses here are easy to understand.

Now, the locations of the seats (*pīṭha*) and so forth for the goddesses are described: In the eight directions of Meru, located in every cardinal and intermediate direction, are all the *pīṭhas*, *upapīṭhas*, *kṣetras*, *chandohas*, *melāpakas*, and *citibhuvanas*, extending from the abode of Vāyu down to the earth of the Buddhas, the sun, and the atoms of embodied beings—of humans, spirits, gods, and asuras. There, the Kulikā wanders for one day by the movement of the sun and moon, acting as the mistress of Śakti.
Regarding the passage beginning with "of Meru" and so forth:
here, in the eight directions of Meru and above, the circle of Yoginīs extends as far as the wind-circle; below, on the earth, their movement is for the sake of sentient beings.

Likewise, it extends to the ocean-circle, the fire-circle, the wind-circle, and up to the limit of space—thus reaching five hundred thousand *yojanas* throughout the mandala of the world-system. Within the bodies of sentient beings, this pervasiveness extends to the tips of the hair, due to the movement of the Blessed One’s Yoginīs.

Here, on the summit of Meru, there is a central lotus (*garbhapadma*) fifty thousand *yojanas* in extent belonging to the Bhagavān, with sixteen petals; its pericarp (*kaṇikā*) is one-third [of that size]. Above the pericarp is the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), and above the sun, upon the sole of the right foot of Kālacakra, is Māra, and upon the sole of the left foot is Kleśa, who is Rudra.
On the eight petals are the eight Vajraḍākinīs, beginning with Dhūmā.
In the intervals between those petals, there are eight skull-cups filled with nectar.

Thus, the sixteen-petaled wheel of bliss consists of the goddess’s skull-cups according to the sixteenfold division of bliss, and the Blessed One has four faces because he bears the four drops (*bindu*). He has twenty-four arms due to the obstruction of the twenty-four fortnights, and he has two more arms than the number of Jinas (twenty-six) due to the obstruction of the fortnights that constitute the intercalary months. He is the aforementioned Vajravega.

The single face of the Bhagavatī is emptiness (*śūnyatā*); her two arms are the signless (*animitta*) and the wishless (*apraṇihita*); and the hand symbols such as the flaying knife and skull-cup are non-conditioning (*anabhisaṃskāra*).

Beyond that lotus, in the cardinal directions of Mount Meru according to the division of the quarters, there is the wheel of the gnosis-element (*jñānadhātu*) with a measurement of twenty-five thousand *yojanas* for the circumference of the earth-circle. On one-third of its ground is a row of flaying knives, and on two-thirds is an eight-spoked wheel;
likewise, in the half of the ocean is the earth-wheel, and in the other half is the water-wheel.
Thus, in the first half of the fire-enclosure is the fire-wheel, and in the second half is the wind-wheel;
likewise, in the first half of the wind-enclosure is the space-wheel, and in the second half is the earth of dust;
and within the space-enclosure are the sixteen cremation grounds—this is the rule.

For here, the body is five cubits from the hairline; by that, there are the external cremation grounds in the sphere of space, and through its purification, the world-system is five hundred thousand *yojanas*. In the *Mahācakrasaṃvara*, thus according to sequence, in the eight directions of Meru within the wheel of the gnosis-element (*jñānadhātucakra*), there are the *pīṭhas*; in the Vimalaprabhā, it is said: "In the cardinal directions, by the cessation of the bow, there are the *upapīṭhas* due to the cessation of old age and death; in the intermediate directions, by the cessation of the scorpion, there is the cessation of birth. Thus, there are two cremation grounds.

Then, on the wheel of the earth element (*pṛthvīdhātucakra*), there are four fields (*kṣetra*) at the cardinal directions through the cessation of the scales (*tulā*) and the cessation of existence (*bhava*);
at the intermediate directions, there are the secondary fields (*upakṣetra*) through the cessation of the virgo (*kanyā*) and the cessation of grasping (*upādāna*).
Thus are the two cremation grounds (*śmaśāna*).
Then, in the water-element wheel, there are four *chandohas* at the cardinal directions through the cessation of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) by means of the cessation of the lion;
and at the intermediate directions, there are *upachandohas* through the cessation of sensation (*vedanā*) by means of the cessation of the crab.
Thus are the two cremation grounds (*śmaśāna*).

Then, in the circle of the fire element (*tejodhātucakra*), there are four meeting points (*melāpaka*) at the cardinal directions through the cessation of the pairs (*mithuna*) and the cessation of contact (*sparśa*);
and at the intermediate directions, there are meeting points through the cessation of Taurus (*vṛṣa*) and the cessation of the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*).
Thus are the two cremation grounds (*śmaśāna*).

Then, in the wind-element wheel, there are four cremation grounds at the cardinal spokes through the cessation of the ram, which is the cessation of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*); and at the intermediate spokes, there are secondary cremation grounds through the cessation of the fish, which is the cessation of consciousness (*vijñāna*). Thus, there are two pairs of cremation grounds.

Then, in the wheel of the space-element (*ākāśadhātu*), there are four *pīlava* dwellings or houses at the cardinal directions through the cessation of formative factors (*saṃskāra*) by means of the cessation of the jar;
and at the intermediate directions, there are the *upapīlava* through the cessation of ignorance (*avidyā*) by means of the cessation of the sea-monster (*makara*).
Thus, there are two cemeteries.
By the cessation of the four junctions (*saṃdhyā*) at the *lagna*, there are another four cremation grounds;
then, by the cessation of the sixteen digits of the moon (*candrakalā*), there are sixteen cremation grounds.
Thus, he possesses the meaning of truth in twelve aspects and is a knower of reality in sixteen aspects.

Through the cessation of the eight watches (prahara), there are eight goddesses; furthermore, through the cessation of the [eight] spokes (*vāra*), according to the Vivṛti, the goddesses in the foundation (*ādhāra*) are unobscured (*nirāvaraṇa*) and have the nature of the supported (*ādheya*). This is from the perspective of ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*). However, from the perspective of worldly convention (*lokasaṃvṛti*), the generation of the mantra-deities in the sacred seats (*pīṭha*) and so forth was taught by the Blessed One in the Root Tantra (*mūlatantra*).
Namely: Kāmarūpa, the seat (pīṭha) called Jāla, Pūrṇagiri, and Oḍḍiyāṇa as the fourth; these are the leading [sites] among the *sl* and *puṣ* syllables.
Then there are the four secondary seats (upapīṭhas): Godāvarī, Rāmeśa, Devikoṭṭa, and Mālava among the *slū*, *pū*, *ṣṛ*, and *śye* syllables.
The Nāyikās reside at Arbuda, Munmunīkṣetra, Oḍra, Kārūṇyapāṭaka,
and Dhidṛthutla; these are the supports for the Goddesses upon the surface of the earth.
Triśakuni is a secondary field (*upakṣetra*), as are Karmārapāṭaka,
Kośala, and the Lāḍa country; in these places, the leaders are of four kinds.
Kaliṅga, Harikela, Chandoha, Candradvīpa, Lampāka, Bhibṛphu, and Plakṣu are the seats where the Nāyikās reside;
likewise, Kāñcī, Koṇaka, Himālaya, and fourthly Nepāla are the Upacchandohas, where the Nāyikās dwell in Plakūba and the others.
Mātṛgṛha, Prayāga, Kollagiri, and Gṛhadevatā constitute the fourfold melāpaka; these are the ḍhiṭhula-nāyikās.
